## Purpose
This document defines the approved Git branching, development, release, and hotfix workflows for Systems Engineering using the GitFlow model. It preserves the original Systems Engineering SOP while adding clarifying structure and visuals. The document is written to be Markdown-first and suitable for PDF generation.

## Scope
- Applies to all Systems Engineering repositories
- Hosted in GitHub Enterprise
- Workflow examples are expressed using Git CLI; all steps are achievable via approved GUI tools

## 1. Prerequisites
- Git installed and configured (CLI)
- Access to GitHub Enterprise
- One or more approved Git clients (GitHub Desktop, TortoiseGit, VS Code, Visual Studio)

---

## 2. Repository Setup

### 2.1 New Repository
```bash
git init
git add .
git commit -m "chore: initial commit"
git branch -M main
git checkout -b develop
git remote add origin https://github.<org>/<repo>.git
git push -u origin main
git push -u origin develop
```

### 2.2 Existing Repository
```bash
git clone https://github.<org>/<repo>.git
cd <repo>
git checkout develop || git checkout -b develop
git pull
```

## 3. GitFlow – Feature-Based Development
The Systems Engineering team will use this model for Git repository branching during development.
Review the diagram and its definitions of the branches.

<!-- EMBED: embeds/figure-1.md -->
![Figure 1](data:image/png;base64,)

**Figure 1: Git **Feature Branch** workflow used during development (feature/* branching, integration to `develop`).**

**Conceptual Notes**
- `main` represents production-ready code
- `develop` is the shared integration branch
- `feature/*` branches are short-lived and scoped to a single unit of work
- Feature work is isolated until reviewed and approved

---

## 4. Development Workflow
This section formalizes the Systems Engineering workflow based upon the Feature-Based development

### Workflow Steps
1. Confirm Git is installed and access to the repository is available
2. Clone the repository
3. Switch to `develop` and pull latest changes
4. Create a feature branch
```bash
git checkout -b feature/<ticket>-<short-desc>
```
5. Make changes and validate locally
6. Commit changes
```bash
git add .
git commit -m "<type>: <description>"
```
7. Sync with `develop`
```bash
git fetch origin
git merge origin/develop
```
8. Resolve conflicts if present
9. Push branch and open a Pull Request targeting `develop`
10. Address review feedback
11. Merge after approval and clean up branch
<!-- pagebreak -->
<div style="page-break-after: always;"></div>

## 5. Release Workflow
Release branches are used to stabilize a version while allowing feature work to continue on `develop`.

<!-- EMBED: embeds/figure-2.md -->
![Figure 2](data:image/png;base64,)

**Figure 2: Git **Release Branch** workflow for stabilizing versions and tagging releases.**

### Release Policy (Mandatory)
- Release branches **must never be merged directly** into `main` or `develop`
- **All merges from a release branch require an approved Pull Request**
- Direct pushes to `main` and `develop` are prohibited

### Release Steps
1. Create a release branch from `develop`
```bash
git checkout develop
git pull
git checkout -b release/<version>
```
2. Perform release hardening (bug fixes, version updates, documentation only)
3. Open a Pull Request to merge `release/<version>` into `main`
4. After PR approval, merge into `main` and tag the release
5. Open a Pull Request to merge `release/<version>` into `develop`
6. Merge only after PR approval to preserve fixes
<!-- pagebreak -->
<div style="page-break-after: always;"></div>

## 6. Hotfix Workflow
Hotfix branches are used to address critical production issues.

<!-- EMBED: embeds/figure-3.md -->
![Figure 3](data:image/png;base64,)

**Figure 3: Git **Hotfix** workflow for urgent fixes from `main`, merged back to `main` and `develop`.**

### Hotfix Policy (Mandatory)
- Hotfix branches are created from `main`
- **All hotfix merges require Pull Requests**
- Hotfix branches **must be merged into both `main` and `develop` via PRs**

### Hotfix Steps
```bash
git checkout main
git pull
git checkout -b hotfix/<version>
```
1. Apply and validate the fix
2. Commit changes
3. Open a Pull Request to merge hotfix into `main`
4. After approval, merge and tag the release
5. Open a Pull Request to merge hotfix into `develop`
6. Merge after approval and delete the hotfix branch

---

## 7. Branch Naming & Protection
- `feature/<ticket>-<description>`
- `release/<version>`
- `hotfix/<version>`

**Protection Rules**
- Protect `main` and `develop`
- Require Pull Requests
- Enforce required reviewers
- Disable force-push

---

## 8. Pull Requests & Reviews
- Keep PRs small and focused
- Clearly describe scope and risk
- Link related work items
- Address feedback through additional commits

---

## 9. Versioning & Tags
Semantic Versioning is required.
```bash
git tag -a v1.2.0 -m "Release 1.2.0"
git push origin --tags
```
